provenance.instrument: Bethel Township Zoning Ordinance of 2008 (Chapter 480 Zoning, Ord. No. 182 of 6-10-2008, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BE2833, Township of Bethel, Delaware County (480-132D(3) and 480-41.3J record plans and deeds in Delaware County, 480-43 refers PRD plans to the Delaware County Planning Commission). District uses and figures are text in each district article. The only attachments are Appendix A and the zoning map. New Laws page: no new laws.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 12-09-2025.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. Among the uses accessory to dwellings in R-1, R-3 and R-4 it lists 'Living quarters for household employees, caretakers, or watchmen' (480-41H(5), 480-47E(5), 480-52I(5), 480-136B(5)). No special exception is named for it, so it reads as a permitted accessory use. The code does not define living quarters or say whether they may have their own kitchen

R-2 (added 2016) lists only a garage, pool, greenhouse and sheds, and offices by special exception, as uses accessory to dwellings. It allows one accessory building of at most 80 sq ft per lot, set 2 ft from the side and rear lines (480-41.4A(7), (8))
The code has no definition of family. A single-family dwelling is 'designed and occupied exclusively as a residence for one family' (480-35)
'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot' (480-35 'Principal building')

Accessory buildings must be 'behind the dwelling or main building' and count toward building coverage. One may stand in one side yard if the side and rear yards are at least 7 ft (480-136, 480-137, 480-41G)

A detached private garage or barn must be 20 ft from the rear of the house, 30 ft from the rear line and 10 ft from a side line. Its height is 16 ft to the peak with a roof pitch of 3 in 12 or more, else 12 ft. Its area limit reads 'eight 860 square feet' in the online text, so the figure is not settled (480-136D)
Minor accessory buildings such as sheds are capped at 200 sq ft and 12 ft (480-136F)
Number of accessory buildings by lot size: 1 under 30,000 sq ft, 2 up to 65,340 sq ft, 3 up to 5 acres, 5 over 5 acres (480-136G)

Conversion of a single-family detached dwelling into a dwelling for more families is a special exception anywhere the general regulations reach. It needs a petition signed by owners of 60% of the frontage within 500 ft, 750 sq ft per unit, lot area per family of at least 75% of the district requirement, no outside change, public water and sewer, and a house 'with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use' (480-138)
Two-family detached dwellings are permitted in R-4 only on a tract of at least 10 acres, with 3,000 sq ft of lot per dwelling, public water and sewer (480-52D, 480-53B, 480-54H)
Up to four nontransient roomers may rent rooms in the house or an accessory building by special exception in R-1, R-3 and R-4 (480-41H(7))

Parking: 3 spaces for every single-family dwelling unit. A fraction rounds up. At least one space must be behind the front building line in residential districts. Living quarters are not listed, so the Zoning Officer applies the most similar use (480-123A, 480-124, 480-125A, B)

Lot of record and nonconforming lots: a building may go on an undersized lot held in separate ownership if it meets the yards, unless the Zoning Hearing Board allows less by special exception (480-131, 480-132D)

Variances: 480-23. No bar on a use variance. Unlisted uses: the district use lists say 'and for no other'. Only LI-1 lets uses 'of the same general natures' as its listed uses in by special exception (480-85D)
Floodplain rules are in Chapter 222 and stream buffers in Chapter 384 (384-24). Trailers may not be used as living quarters (Chapter 419)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Bethel Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Article II (480-5 to 480-24), Article IV (480-31 to 480-35), Article V, Articles VI to XIII, XV and XVI (district use and area rules, M-H read in full), Article XVIII (parking, by screen view), Article XIX 480-130 to 480-149 (text cut off within 480-149), Chapter 222 sections 16 and 27, Chapter 384 section 24, the New Laws page and code searches. Not read: Article I, Article III, Article XVII signs, Article XX, 480-149.1 and 480-149.2, Chapter 239 historic preservation, the rest of Chapters 222 and 384, and Chapter 395.

term.note: Not called an accessory dwelling. Listed among the uses accessory to dwellings. Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, domestic employee, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters and conversion

status.note: Quarters only for household employees, caretakers or watchmen, not relatives and never a tenant. A permitted accessory use with no hearing named

status_outside.note: R-2, C-1, C-2, LI-1, T and M-H do not list living quarters. Of these only R-2 permits single-family houses

path.note: Listed as a use accessory to dwellings without the words 'by special exception' that items (7) and (8) carry. A zoning permit

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, on the usual findings. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into a dwelling for more families
value.conditions: Petition signed by owners of 60% or more of the frontage on the street within 500 ft. Each unit at least 750 sq ft. Lot area per family at least 75% of the district requirement. District yards and building area met. No outside change except for safety. Parking met. Only for a house 'with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use'. Public water and public sewer. The Board sets the number of families

requires.condition: Petition of owners of 60% of the frontage within 500 ft, and a finding that the house has little economic usefulness as a single-family home

value.note: Lot minimums for two families read as twice 75% of the district lot with public services: 2 x 22,500 sq ft in R-1, R-3 and R-4, 2 x 7,500 sq ft in R-2

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (R-4)
value.conditions: Permitted in R-4 on a tract of at least 10 acres, at most six dwelling units per acre. Lot area 3,000 sq ft per dwelling and width 60 ft. Front yard 25 ft, two side yards of 25 ft together and 10 ft each, rear yard 25 ft, coverage 30%, height 35 ft. Public water and public sewer
value.note: A new two-family building on a tract of 10 acres or more, not a unit added to a house

historic_bypass.note: No historic path found in the zoning chapter. Chapter 239 was not read

value.condition: The quarters are only for household employees, caretakers or watchmen of the household. The code does not let them be rented to others.
Quarters in a separate building must be an accessory building, not a second house. 'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot.'

The number of accessory buildings is capped by lot size: one on a lot under 30,000 sq ft, two from 30,000 to 65,340 sq ft, three up to 5 acres and five over 5 acres. The third and later ones need 50 ft from other buildings. A lot that already has its allowed accessory buildings has no room for a new one.

In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a DEP permit. The floodplain chapter bars hospitals, nursing homes, jails and new manufactured home parks, not houses.

Where a stream or a lake, pond or wetland is on the site, the stormwater chapter asks for a planted riparian buffer of 50 ft from the top of bank. On a lot that existed when the chapter was adopted it may be 25% of the side or rear setback or 25 ft, whichever is greater. Only trails, utility lines, bridges and other uses the Township approves may be in it.
